Hi Alex —

Thanks again for the interest and for lining up the broader BrightBank team. We have a 60-minute technical demo ready and I proposed a few time slots in the invite. One wrinkle we spotted internally: EU and US DST rollbacks are staggered this season (EU moves back a week earlier than the US), which creates a one-week window where the usual overlaps between CET and ET shift by an hour. Since your APAC colleagues also want to join, we want to pick a time that keeps latency-sensitive walkthroughs within reasonable local hours for all parties.

Quick asks: can you confirm whether BrightBank will follow CET for scheduling (your calendar invites default to CET) or if people will be accepting invites in their local TZs? Second, can your calendar admin check whether any recurring rules will auto-adjust in that one-week window (we've seen some org calendars reapply offsets that break multi-region invites).

I've attached a quick slot matrix with alternatives (Rough-slot-matrix.csv). Proposed: 2026-11-02 10:00 ET / 15:00 CET (tight for APAC but still okay) or 2026-10-29 09:00 ET / 14:00 CET (before US rollback). If neither works, we can do two shorter sessions: one for US/EU and a brief overlap for APAC.

If it's helpful I can draft a short mutual action plan (roles, agenda, recording permissions) and a fallback plan in case someone is moved by their calendar service.

Cheers,

Hi Ben —

Thanks for the heads-up. BrightBank uses CET as the canonical timezone for team invites in EMEA; however, individual acceptances often keep local offsets so we do get the one-week mismatch you're describing. Our internal policy is to not change recurring rules for short-term meetings, so invites scheduled before the EU rollback generally keep local conversions and can shift participants by an hour relative to each other during the mismatch week.

Maya here (cc) is our meetings coordinator — we've checked the calendars for the core list and 2026-10-29 at 14:00 CET (your proposed pre-rollback slot) works for the EMEA attendees. The US folks are likely to see that as 09:00 ET. For the US rollback week (2026-11-02), some attendees will see the 10:00 ET slot as 15:00 CET and others as 14:00 CET due to client-side conversions.

Best practice on our side: schedule a single event at the time that is correct for the majority and include explicit local-times in the invite description (e.g., "2026-11-02 — 10:00 ET / 15:00 CET / 00:00 IST"). We can also send a reminder with timezone-aware text 24 hours prior.

Maya: can you confirm whether APAC will join live? If not, we'll prioritize US/EU live overlap.

— Calendar Admin
